source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

hinge.title: Decide how to construct a 90 degree angle at a point on a line by first making that point the midpoint of a segment on the line.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: A 90 degree angle is formed at O is what produces choose X and Y equidistant from O on the line, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about Decide how to construct a 90 degree angle at a point on.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: The given line rule also covers this: constructing a perpendicular from a point outside a line, so it is not an exception — on the item about Decide how to construct a 90 degree angle at a point on.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: given line is settled by running 'Decide how to construct exact 60 degree, 30 degree, and 15 degree': A 60 degree angle is obtained by constructing an equilateral triangle from equal-radius — on the item about Decide how to construct a 90 degree angle at a point on.

intelligence.enrichment: To construct a perpendicular at point O on a line, mark points X and Y on the line at equal distances from O so that O is the midpoint of XY; the perpendicular bisector of XY then passes through O and is perpendicular to the line.
